definition: A controlled vocabulary provides a way to organize knowledge for subsequent retrieval.
details: Controlled vocabularies are used in subject indexing schemes, subject headings, thesauri, taxonomies, and other knowledge organization systems. Controlled vocabulary schemes mandate the use of predefined, preferred terms that have been preselected by the designers of the schemes, in contrast to natural language vocabularies, which have no such restriction.

explainer.lead: A controlled vocabulary is an agreed list of preferred terms for describing information so it can be found again. By making indexers use the same wording, it reduces the chance that related material becomes scattered under different labels.

tiers.eli5: Imagine everyone putting photos into boxes, but one person writes “dogs,” another writes “puppies,” and someone else writes “pet animals.” A controlled vocabulary is like a shared label sheet that tells everyone which label to use. That makes it much easier to find all the photos that belong together.
tiers.practitioner: Use a controlled vocabulary when indexing records through subject headings, thesauri, taxonomies, or similar knowledge organization systems. Configure the indexing workflow to accept predefined preferred terms rather than unrestricted natural-language labels. A common pitfall is letting indexers introduce their own wording, which weakens consistency and can split related records across terms.
tiers.paperLevel: A controlled vocabulary can be represented as a predefined set V of preferred terms selected by the designers of a knowledge organization scheme; indexing must use terms from V. This differs from natural-language vocabularies, where term choice is not restricted in this way.

explainer.example: Suppose a subject indexing scheme includes “controlled vocabulary” as its preferred term. An indexer describing an article about approved word lists must use “controlled vocabulary” rather than creating a separate label such as “approved word list,” keeping the article with material indexed under the same term.

explainer.intuition: Retrieval works better when everyone describes similar material with the same approved words. A controlled vocabulary trades freedom of wording for consistency.
howItWorks: The scheme’s designers preselect a set of preferred terms.
The scheme mandates those terms instead of allowing unrestricted natural-language wording.
Indexers apply the preferred terms when describing material.
The resulting organized descriptions support subsequent retrieval.
explainer.whyItMatters: Without a shared restriction on terms, different indexers can describe the same subject in different ways. Controlled vocabularies organize those descriptions consistently so that later retrieval is less dependent on guessing each indexer’s wording.
misconceptions: It is not a ban on particular words in ordinary writing; the restriction applies within the vocabulary scheme.
It is not an unrestricted collection of natural-language terms; its preferred terms are predefined and preselected.
It is not limited to one format: it can be used in subject headings, thesauri, taxonomies, and other systems.
